chunks: 958 - And he, peace be upon him, used to say between the two evening prayers:

"O Allah, in Your hand are the measures of the night and the day, the measures of the world and the Hereafter, the measures of death and life, the measures of the sun and the moon, the measures of victory and abandonment, and the measures of wealth and poverty. O Allah, repel from me the evil of the sinful among the jinn and humankind, and make my return to lasting good and bliss that does not pass away."

key_terms.فَسَقَةِ: the sinful and defiantly disobedient ones
key_terms.مَقَادِيرُ: the measured decrees and apportionments of all things
key_terms.مُنْقَلَبِي: my return, final turning, or eventual outcome
key_terms.ٱلْخِذْلَانِ: forsaking, abandonment, or failure of support

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام supplicate between Maghrib and Isha about Allah’s decree and protection from evil?
ai.summary: This supplication affirms that all measures and decrees of existence belong to Allah, including time, life, death, victory, and provision. It teaches the supplicant to seek refuge from evil influences among jinn and humans, and to ask for an ultimate return to enduring good and everlasting bliss.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.958 - He (Imam Al-Sadiq) used to say between the Maghrib and Isha prayers:

Allahumma biyadika maqadeeru al-layli wa an-nahar, wa maqadeeru ad-dunya wa al-akhirah, wa maqadeeru al-mawti wa al-hayah, wa maqadeeru ash-shamsi wa al-qamar, wa maqadeeru an-Nasri wa al-khidhlan, wa maqadeeru al-ghina wa al-faqr. Allahumma idra’ ‘anni sharra fasaqati al-jinni wa al-ins, wa aj‘al munqalabi ila khayrin da’imin wa na‘eemin la yazool
"O’ Allah (swt), in Your hands are the measures of night and day, the measures of this world and the Hereafter, the measures of death and life, the measures of the sun and the moon, the measures of victory and defeat, and the measures of wealth and poverty. O’ Allah (swt), keep away from me the evil of the disobedient among jinn and humans, and make my eventual return one of perpetual goodness and everlasting bliss."
